title: marko-ui acceptance scenarios
description: One file describing every acceptance scenario for the published marko-ui CLI: real scaffolders, real package managers, real projects. Consumed by e2e/acceptance/scripts/validate-scenarios.ts and, once the runner lands, by the vitest suite.

helpers.description: Named helper programs the runner executes via a `{command: "@helper", helper: <name>}` step. A helper exists so that a scenario says WHAT it is building, not which shell incantation builds it: the runner dev implements each helper once, in one language, from the contract in `description` plus `source`.

bodies.description: Named multi-line strings (file bodies, shell scripts) reused by pre-steps, so a scenario stays readable.

fixtures.description: Named, reusable project scaffolds. A scenario either names one with setup.fixture or inlines its own setup.scaffold.

flows.description: Named, reusable step sequences. A step may be `use: <flow>` to splice a whole flow in at that position.

cliTarget.description: How the CLI under test is obtained. `published` = `marko-ui@<version>` from npm; `tarball` = `bun pack`ed from this repo and installed from the .tgz. Overridable per scenario with setup.cliTarget.

version.description: npm version used when cliTarget is `published`. `latest` tracks dist-tags.

tag.description: key:value tag. `os` and `pm` drive the CI matrix; `kind` and `speed` drive sharding. `needs:<branch-or-gate>` marks a scenario whose expectation depends on behaviour that is not merged yet: the runner SKIPS it (reported, not failed) while the gate is unlanded, and the CI job that runs it is keyed on the same tag. Free-form keys are allowed but the runner only knows these five.

pm.description: Which real package manager drives installs and CLI invocation. `yarn-classic` and `yarn-berry` are separate: they differ in runner (`npx` fallback vs `yarn dlx`) and lockfile.

network.description: What the scenario needs reachable, counting setup (scaffold + install) as well as steps. `none`: the scenario passes with ALL egress blocked. `registry-only`: the registry host must answer; nothing is installed from npm during the scenario, so npm may be blocked (registry-health scenarios that only issue HTTP). `npm`: npm must answer; the registry is unreachable or never consulted (the registry-down scenarios point REGISTRY_URL at a dead port). `both`: both must answer — this is the default for anything that runs `init` or `add` on a really-installed project, because init fetches the style item from the registry AND installs @tailwindcss/vite + tw-animate-css from npm.

node.description: Node majors the scenario is meaningful on. A scenario with no `node` runs on the CI default only.

tools.description: Binaries that must be on PATH. The runner skips (does not fail) a scenario whose tool is missing, and reports it as skipped.

fixture.description: Name from the top-level `fixtures` map. Mutually exclusive with `scaffold`.

scaffold.description: An inline real scaffolder run. `tool` is the bin, `args` its arguments (the runner prefixes the right dlx runner per pm), `dir` is the subdirectory the app lands in, relative to the scenario workspace.

install.description: Run the scaffold's own dependency install with `pm`. false means the scenario wants an uninstalled scaffold (rare, and only with a post-step that installs).

noScaffold.description: The workspace starts empty: no scaffolder runs at all (the `empty-dir` case, and the registry-health scenarios that only make HTTP requests).

cliTarget.description: Override defaults.cliTarget for this scenario (used by the tarball sweep).

post.description: Applied after `install`, before the first CLI step.

preStep.description: A mutation applied to the project before any CLI command runs. Exactly one verb per step.

write.description: Create or replace a file. `content` may be a literal string or a named fixture body.

body.description: Alternative to `content`: a named string from the top-level `bodies` map, resolved by the runner before writing.

cp.description: Copy a scaffolded file or directory to another path. Used by pre-steps that build a monorepo layout out of a single scaffold.

run.description: A shell command run in the scenario workspace. Real tools only — no stubs.

body.description: Alternative to `cmd`: a named script from the top-level `bodies` map.

helper.description: Run a named helper from the top-level `helpers` map. The pre-step form of `{command: "@helper"}` — setup builds project shapes (monorepo layouts, a relocatable config) with the same documented programs the steps use, so each helper has one implementation and one contract. `cwd` defaults to the helper's own declared default.

args.description: Literal argv for the helper. Same closed `$VAR` set as a step's `args`.

cwd.description: Working directory for this pre-step, relative to the scenario workspace.

stdinMode.description: closed = /dev/null or an immediately-EOF pipe; null = inherited closed pipe the runner never writes; piped = a pipe the runner writes `stdin` into then closes; pty = a real pseudo-terminal driven by `pty`.

use.description: Splice in a named flow from the top-level `flows` map at this position.

command.description: Top-level marko-ui command, or an @-prefixed runner operation (see README §Operations).

sub.description: Subcommand path under `command`, e.g. ["sync"] for `agents sync`, ["list"] for `registry list`. Flags belong in `args`, not here.

args.description: Literal argv. `$VAR` is interpolated by the runner from a FIXED, closed set, so a scenario can never smuggle in an undefined variable: $WORKSPACE (absolute scenario workspace), $APP (absolute fixture app dir), $PM (the scenario's package manager name), $REGISTRY_URL (defaults.registryUrl, or the ACCEPTANCE_REGISTRY_URL override), $ACCEPTANCE_MIRROR_PORT (the port the scenario's local registry mirror is served on). A literal `$` is written `$$`. Unknown `$VAR` is a validation error, not an empty string.

helper.description: Name from the top-level `helpers` map. Required by, and only valid with, `command: "@helper"`. The runner executes the helper's `source` with the step's `args` as its argv, from the step's cwd, and with the same five variables the step walker exports into the environment ($WORKSPACE, $APP, $PM, $REGISTRY_URL, $ACCEPTANCE_MIRROR_PORT) — several helpers read process.env.APP to locate the scaffolded app rather than depending on their cwd for it.

cwd.description: Where to run the step, relative to the scenario workspace. `.` is the workspace root; the fixture's app dir is named explicitly (usually `app`). DEFAULT: the fixture's app dir, or the workspace root when the fixture has none (`noScaffold`).

runner.description: How the CLI binary is invoked. Omit to use the scenario's pm default (bunx / npx -y / pnpm dlx / yarn dlx).

cliVersion.description: Pin this step to a specific published version ("0.4.1") instead of defaults.version. The upgrade scenario uses it to initialize a project with the previous release; every other step must omit it.

pty.description: Pseudo-terminal answer script for interactive runs. Each entry waits for `expect` to appear in the merged output, then types `send`. The runner fails the step if `expect` never appears (with a 30 s cap).

env.description: Extra environment for this step only. `null` unsets a variable inherited from the scenario env.

offline.description: Run THIS ONE step with egress to both the registry and npm blocked. It is a per-step switch and says nothing about the rest of the scenario, so it is legal in a scenario whose requires.network is `both` — env.offline-no-skill runs init and add live against the registry and cuts only the final agents sync. Contradictory uses are rejected by check:acceptance: `offline: true` on an `@http` step, or on a step whose args interpolate $REGISTRY_URL.

pathWithout.description: Run this one step with these binaries removed from PATH, by putting a PATH whose entries exclude them first. Replaces the old magic `PATH_NO_GIT=1` env var.

snapshot.description: After this step succeeds, record a content hash of each of these paths (relative to the step's cwd) in the scenario's snapshot table. A later `expect.unchanged` compares against it. Replaces the `shasum` + hand-written `.agents-sync.sha` convention.

description.description: The CONTRACT, in one short paragraph: what the helper guarantees to have done when it exits 0. The runner dev implements from this plus `source`; a reviewer reads this alone.

language.description: `node` sources run under the scenario's node with no flags. `posix-shell` sources run under `sh`. There is no third option, deliberately: the helpers exist because eleven near-identical inline `node -e` programs were unreadable, not to introduce a build step.

cwd.description: DEFAULT cwd when a step invoking this helper does not set one. Relative to the scenario workspace. Note the overall default (the fixture's app dir) does NOT apply to a helper that declares its own cwd: a helper scoped to the workspace root (".") says so here, and check:acceptance then REQUIRES every invocation to restate `cwd: "."` at the call site — inheriting the app-dir default would run the program one level too deep, which is exactly how make-bun-workspace would move the app into itself.

expect.description: What the step must produce. All listed assertions must hold; nothing unlisted is asserted.

exit.description: Exact exit code, or a set of accepted codes. The CLI documents 0/1/2/3/4.

stdoutMatches.description: Regex sources matched against stdout with ANSI escapes stripped (the repo's proto shim injects NO_COLOR=1 — never assert on color).

filesExist.description: Paths (relative to the step's cwd) that must exist. A trailing `/**` matches recursively.

jsonPath.description: RFC 6901 pointer assertions against a JSON file (components.json, skills-lock.json), or against the step's own stdout with `source: stdout` (where `path` is omitted).

pointer.description: JSON pointer. Empty string means the document root.

equals.description: Deep-equal expected value, or the string "<exists>" to assert only that the pointer resolves to anything.

appBuild.description: Run the project's own build script with its own package manager and assert the outcome.

appRender.description: Start the built server on a free port, fetch one route, assert the markup, stop it.

unchanged.description: Each path (relative to the step's cwd) must have exactly the content it had when an earlier step's `snapshot:` recorded it. This is how the idempotence assertions work — no shasum, no committed .sha file.

changed.description: Each path (relative to the step's cwd) must NOT match the content snapshotted for it earlier — the inverse of `unchanged`.

dirExists.description: A directory (relative to the step's cwd) must exist. Distinct from filesExist, which must NOT match a directory.

noop.description: Assert nothing but the exit code. Exists for the rare step whose observable outcome is recorded for a human rather than asserted; prefer a real assertion.

id.description: Stable, unique, dot-namespaced id. CI filters and replay use it verbatim.

kind.description: The KIND of user situation this represents. Two scenarios of the same kind must not both exist — the runner's coverage argument is 'one scenario per kind of situation, not per product'.

env.description: Environment for every step in this scenario.

cwd.description: Default step cwd for the whole scenario. Defaults to the fixture's app dir.

speed.description: Rough wall-clock class, from the measured table in README §Timing. `fast` ≤ ~2 min, `medium` ≤ ~6 min, `slow` > 6 min (a real install-heavy or Node-matrix scenario).

ci.description: CI placement. Windows runs report but never block: windows-blocking stays false everywhere.

nightlyOnly.description: Runs in the nightly job, not the per-push blocking job (Node matrices, slow monorepo sweeps).

status.description: `specified` (the default): asserted normally. `unknown-expectation`: the expected behaviour could not be determined from the code — reported, not asserted, until a human answers `question`. `needs-cli-guards`: the behaviour IS settled and the expectation is written down, but it depends on a guard that has not landed yet (see the `needs:` tag) — reported and SKIPPED, never failed, until the guard lands. `known-bug`: the expectation is correct and the CLI does not meet it — a real defect, recorded in `bug` — reported and SKIPPED, never failed and never quietly weakened, until the bug is fixed. The three non-defaults are three different situations and the distinction is the point: an unknown expectation is a QUESTION for a human, a needs-guards expectation is a KNOWN ANSWER waiting on code, and a known-bug is a KNOWN ANSWER that the code does not meet.

question.description: Required when status is unknown-expectation: the exact question to the CLI owner, with the scenario id.

bug.description: Required when status is known-bug: the tracking id (a beads id, an issue URL) or a one-line repro. This is the record that keeps the scenario's expectation intact while the defect it found is open — the scenario is SKIPPED with this text, so the bug is reported on every run instead of being deleted, inverted, or relaxed until it passes.

covers.description: The axis entries this scenario is the representative for (free text; used to build the coverage table in the README).
